findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed that the back door was letting in some daylight at the bottom, indicating that the door was not tight-fitting as to protect against the entry of insects. PIC was informed and stated that there was a previous protective piece in place that is no longer there, and will work on getting it replaced by the next routine inspection. Ensure that outer openings of food establishments protect against entry of pests by filling gaps and having tight-fitting exterior doors.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed employees that were cleaning (or doing other tasks) put on gloves to prepare foods without handwashing first. The PIC was instructed to educate employees about washing hands before donning gloves to engage in food preparation. Ensure that employees always wash hands before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the front hand washing sink and customer bathrooms do not have ‘employees must wash hands before returning to work’ signs. The inspector provided signage to the PIC. Ensure that all hand washing sinks always have proper signage that notify employees to wash hands.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed eggs stored on the top shelf of the double cooler over various ready-to-eat foods. The PIC was notified and they moved the eggs onto the bottom shelf. Ensure that raw foods are always stored below ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTIONS ON 7/28/2023, 3/7/2023, 7/22/2022 (Noted in comments), 1/21/2022, and 5/8/2023. A NOTICE TO COMPLY WILL BE ISSUED AND ADDITIONAL VIOLATIONS WILL RESULT IN INCREASED ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO POSSIBLE SUSPENSION OF PERMIT. 

This is the 5th inspection since the 2017 FDA Food Code was adopted in 2019 that the facility has been without a certified food manager. A certified food manager must be present at ALL TIMES when food preparation/service is occurring in the facility. The current person-in-charge is new to the position and states that certification is planned. Ensure that a certified food manager is present during all operational hours. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.comment:

Dented cans must be separated/returned prior to being stocked in and MAY NOT be used in food service. Ensure that staff are checking cans at delivery or prior to stocking and that cans with significant dents along upper/lower or side seams are removed immediately. Inspector will return on 12/26/2023 to check cans in the facility at that time.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The facility used chlorine sanitizer throughout the kitchen. Two buckets of sanitizer solution were prepared for use. Both of these buckets had chlorine concentrations below 50 ppm. Chlorine concentration must be at least 100 ppm for proper sanitizing of food-contact surfaces in the facility. Bleach was added to the buckets bringing the concentrations into compliance. Corrected on site. Ensure that chlorine concentration is tested an sufficiently concentrated at all times. Consider placing wiping cloths in the bucket prior to adding chlorine to prevent excess absorption by the cloths. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

This sink must be re-caulked or otherwise sealed. findings.comment: 2-301.12: Operator was observed washing his hands but used his bare hands to turn off the water and then grab a paper towel. Advised on proper procedures and operator confirmed understanding. Ensure all employees are washing their hands properly each time. (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: 3-302.11: A can opener was observed resting on a shelf between the food prep area and front of the store. The shelf itself was soiled with debris. The can opener was removed from the shelf and the shelf itself was cleaned and sanitized so that it may be stored there. Operator stored a thermometer in a cup with pens and other non-food items that was visibly soiled. The thermometer did not have a cover. Thermometer was moved to a container which is clean and did not have other non-food items in it. (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: 3-501.16: Probe temperature taken of meatballs in hot holding was observed to have temperatures ranging from 119 F to 142 F depending on location in the container. Operator stated that food temperature was turned down during lunch rush but is in the process of reheating. TCS food must be maintained above 135 degrees unless cooling for storage and temperatures must be checked to ensure they reach appropriate temperatures. (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. No employees at the facility have completed allergen training. Allergen training must be completed by next inspection as required. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Multiple priority violations were observed during inspection that included handwashing (when, where, and how to properly wash hands), proper glove use, hot and cold holding temperatures, and sanitization. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection.
 Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Shift manager that was PIC at the time of inspection did not have proof of a food manager certification. Manager indicated they had a certification through their previous employer, but they are also registered to take a food manager course on 1/30/22 to complete certification. Store manager with certification returned to the facility during inspection and stated they would remain on-site through the end of the current business day. Ensure that enough managers have CFMs to cover all hours of operation. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) One of the food employees working at the time of inspection did not have a signed reporting agreement on file. Employee health policy was discussed, and employee signed a copy of the reporting agreement during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employees were observed putting on gloves without first washing their hands. Employees were previously observed preparing a sanitizer solution and handling their cell phone. 
Another employee that arrived to work clocked in and then immediately put on gloves at the prep table without first washing their hands. When employee was approached about washing their hands a comment was made about washing their hands at home. Employee was advised hands must be washed upon arriving at work prior to food handling.
Employees were advised on when to wash hands, and employees were observed making the effort to wash hands more consistently between tasks for remainder of inspection. Educational handout on when to wash hands was provided.
 Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed upon entering the work area at the start of shift, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier, and paper towels were manually dispensed after water was shut off. Proper technique was discussed, and educational handout was provided.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Employee that just arrived to work was advised to wash their hands prior to assisting with food prep and was observed walking back to the 3 part. Employee then went to the handwashing sink in the prep area after inspector stated handwashing needs to occur at a designated handwashing sink. Ensure all staff are properly trained to wash hands only at designated handwashing sinks.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee answered the phone with gloved hands and proceeded up front to continue with food prep without a changing gloves. Proper use of gloves was discussed. Employee washed hands prior to putting on new gloves. Educational handout on proper glove use was provided.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Bleach solution in freshly made sani-bucket was 0ppm. Shift manager added a very small amount of bleach to prepare the solution initially. Manager was advised on proper concentration for product and added more bleach to bring the concentration to 200pppm. 
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Ensure bleach solutions are maintained at 200ppm per the label directions, and use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A) (1) Soups in the left warmer were observed with internal temperatures of 131F (pumpkin) and 125 (jerk chicken). The warmer was almost out of water, and the add water light indicator was on. The temperature dial was also at the lowest setting. Water was added to the unit, and temperature dial was put on highest setting to reheat soups to 165F. Manager was advised to discard any leftover portions of the aforementioned soups at the end of operations.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A) (2) Internal temperatures for foods in the top and bottom holding areas of the prep cooler were observed at 48F-50F on the left end of the cooler. Chicken salad, Fajita chicken, and pepperoni on the far left side in the top of the cooler were at 48.5F-49F. Ham more toward the middle in the top holding area was at 46.5F-47F, and mayo on the far right side of the top left holding area was at 44F. Veggie meatballs in the bottom on the far left side of the cooler were at 50F. Sliced tomatoes in the top right side of the prep cooler had an internal temperature of 44F. Roast beef and chicken salad had internal temperatures of 44F-45F in the middle and right side in the bottom holding area. Foods above 45F were discarded and switched out with fresh product. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Prep cooler was not holding consistent temperature. TCS foods were observed with internal temperatures ranging from 44F to 50F depending on location within the cooler (see #22 for details). Manager was advised to store food in the 2 door cooler overnight and only maintain what is needed during operational hours in the bottom of the prep cooler toward the right side. Manager was also advised to monitor internal temperatures and use time control for working supplies of TCS foods in the top left holding area until the prep cooler is serviced and able to maintain foods at 41F/below. Time controlled foods must be served or discarded within 4hrs and cannot be placed back in the other cooler after 4hr time limit. Monitor foods in the top right holding area as well and use time control if that side appears to also have issues maintaining temperature.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15 Gap remains to be corrected under the back door. Manager has a plan to purchase weather stripping to make repairs. 
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 Small white bugs (possibly mold mites) were observed at the corner of a damaged, loose floor tile and around drain line plumbing where mold buildup was present adjacent to the recessed floor drain under the 3 part sink (see #55 for additional information). Manager began cleaning the area with bleach water to remove buildup and eliminate pests. No apparent pest activity was observed under the loose floor tile after cleaning where small white bugs were observed. Manager was encouraged to speak with owners about having pest control operator come in for service if any additional activity is observed.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.122 Floor under the 3 part sink next to the drain was cleaned since the routine inspection. Upon closer inspection during spot check some buildup was present around the drain line plumbing within the floor adjacent to the floor drain. One of the floor tiles next to the drain was loose and had a small piece broken off at the corner. Manager cleaned under the 3 part sink during inspection. Ensure proper repairs are made to replace and/or seal tiles under the 3 part sink. 
 Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair and be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A) (2) Tuna salad in the top holding area of the prep cooler had an internal temperature of 47F. Tuna salad in the bottom of the prep cooler was also observed at 46F-47F. Tuna in the bottom of the cooler was moved to the 2 door cooler for cold holding. Tuna in the top holding area was to be served or discarded by the close of business today. 
-Portions of TCS foods were stacked above the fill line of containers in the top holding area of the prep cooler and were observed at temperatures ranging from 48F-51F. Foods included, but were not necessarily limited to, pastrami, cheese slices, and roast beef. Internal temperatures of foods were observed at 43F-45F in the top of the prep cooler. Portions above the fill line were removed and discarded.
NOTE: The cooler was holding around 43F-44F and dropped to 40F-41F after the thermostat was adjusted to a colder setting. (See general comments for additional information)
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15 Light was visible under the back door. A gap was present due to the absence of weather stripping. Provide weather stripping to eliminate the gap under the back door. 
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor under the 3 part sink next to the drain was soiled with black, grimy buildup. Clean the floor under the 3 part sink next to the drain.
-Back prep area handwashing sink had pink mold accumulation in the basin drain. Clean the handwashing sinks as needed and maintain them clean.  
 Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text:
5-103.12 - Hot water is still not available at the back handsink. PIC stated the owners are aware of the issue and have a call in for service. In the meantime, the hot water line remains shut off until repairs are completed. (see general comments for additional information).
Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Shift manager that was PIC at the time of inspection had proof of a food handler certification but not a manager certification. A CFM was not present during the inspection. Ensure that enough managers have CFMs to cover all hours of operation. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to prepare a customer's order. Just prior to putting on gloves the manager was on the phone. Handwashing between tasks and prior to putting on gloves to handle food were discussed. PIC washed his hands and put on a new pair of gloves. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sanitizer solution at 3 part sink was observed at ~100ppm chlorine. The product used at the facility requires a concentration of 200ppm per the label directions. The solution in question was made earlier in the day. Solution in question was discarded, and a fresh solution at 200ppm chlorine was prepared. 
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Ensure bleach solutions are maintained at 200ppm per the label directions, and use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Surfaces in the ice shoot and above the dispensing nozzle were soiled with buildup on the freestyle machine. Ice shoot and dispenser housing were cleaned during the inspection. Clean and sanitize the ice shoot, the dispensing nozzle, and the surface above the nozzle daily/as needed to eliminate buildup. 
Equipment such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Sani-bucket solution was observed at proper concentration but was soiled with food debris and visible soil. Solution was prepared earlier in the day and was changed.
Chemical sanitizing solutions in which wet wiping cloths are held between uses shall be free of food debris and visible soil. Ensure sanitizer solution is changed as needed throughout the day once the solution becomes soiled and/or the concentration weakens.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text:
5-103.12 Hot water is not available at the back handsink. The hot water line is shut off. When it is turned on, the hot water runs non-stop. PIC was advised both hot and cold water under pressure must be available at all fixtures. Fix the plumbing at the back handsink so that hot water is available at all times and not turned off.
Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. One of the employees working at the time of inspection had a food allergen awareness certification, but their shift ended halfway through the inspection. The shift manager did not have a food allergen awareness certification. A certified food manager with an allergen awareness certification must be on-site at all hours of operation. 
 Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: 3-501.16: (A) (2) Food in the double door cooler was not cold held properly at 41 F. All food in the cooler that was probed had temperatures between 48 and 58 F. All TCS foods inside the cooler that were dated before 8-3-20 were discarded. Additionally, all TCS food that had been delivered to the facility in the double door cooler dated 8/3/20 may be used or discarded within 6 hours (by 3:00 pm). All TCS food must be cold held at 41 F or below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: 4-301.11: The double door cooler was observed maintaining a temperature of 58 F. The cooler did not have sufficient cooling capacity to cold hold food. All coolers which cold hold food must have the capacity to hold food at 41 F or below. The manager stated that a new cooler will be delivered to the facility tomorrow (8-14).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed R-I Cooler to have damaged seal. Ensure equipment is in proper repair. In addition, ensure food equipment is easily cleanable. Reference 4-501.11.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: No test strips available for sanitizer. Ensure test strips are available for proper testing of chemical. Reference 4-302.14

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: REPEAT #2: No allergen awareness certification was provided during inspection. All CFMs working in category I restaurants must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program. Reference PA 100-0367.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
REPEAT #1: No allergen certification can be provided by PIC. All CFMs must be allergen certified 
PA 100-0367. All certified food protection managers (CFPMs) working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment: No documentation was provided regarding employee health for employees. Corrected. Handout Provided.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(17) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of responsibilities for preventing the transmission of foodborne disease and exclusion or restriction of Food Employees. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(17).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment: No documentation was provided for clean-up. Corrected. Handout Provided.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11  (Pf) Establishment does not have procedures for employees to follow when responding to discharging of vomitus or fecal matter. Provide procedures to comply with this section of the code. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
PIC does not have food allergen training. Allergen training is required for all category I facilities.
PA 100-0367: All CFMs working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.
